findings.evidence: "Fig 6.1: The metric hierarchy as a diagnostic chain [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] — a conceptual schematic; the three-layer grouping is a framing choice, not a measured classification. ... Label caveat: a concurrency entry in the workload box denotes the request rate λ that the traffic offers, not a concurrency value — request concurrency is derived on the serving side (in-flight = λ × W, Little’s law), the same classification this figure gives queue depth."
findings.issue: The figure itself includes 'concurrency' inside the workload-metrics box, while the chapter text repeatedly states that concurrency is not a workload input and belongs on the serving/scheduler side. The caption tries to rescue the label by redefining it as 'request rate λ', but that is exactly the kind of reused term with two meanings that the chapter warns against. A reader scanning the figure alone will infer that concurrency is a workload metric.
findings.fix_instruction: Remove 'concurrency' from the workload box in Fig 6.1 and label the box 'rps · token profile (λ)'. If λ must appear, label it 'offered rate λ' rather than 'concurrency'. Keep the Little's-law derivation in the serving/scheduler layer only.

findings.page: PDF p. 146 (printed p. 122); governing text at PDF p. 145 (printed p. 121)
findings.evidence: §6.1.1 (PDF p. 145): "Concurrency is not a workload input: it is a serving-side quantity derived from the arrival rate and the time in system (Little's law), so it belongs with queue depth on the scheduler side, not in this layer."  Figure 6.1's top box (PDF p. 146) nevertheless reads "Workload metrics / rps · token profile · concurrency", and the caption admits the mismatch: "Label caveat: a concurrency entry in the workload box denotes the request rate λ that the traffic offers, not a concurrency value — request concurrency is derived on the serving side (in-flight = λ × W, Little's law), the same classification this figure gives queue depth; see §6.1.1."
findings.issue: Figure 6.1's Workload-metrics box lists 'concurrency' as a workload metric, which directly contradicts the chapter's own classification in §6.1.1 (concurrency is serving-side, derived via Little's law). The caption tries to repair the figure by re-defining the box label to mean something else ('concurrency' = arrival rate λ), so the figure's printed text and its caption say different things about the same word. A reader reading the figure alone will log concurrency as a workload metric, which is exactly the population-vs-occupancy conflation Ch 4 §4.5 warns against. Note that the caption handles queue depth correctly ('queue depth: scheduler state, not a serving metric'), so the defect is confined to the concurrency entry.
findings.fix_instruction: Edit the Figure 6.1 Workload-metrics box to replace 'concurrency' with 'arrival rate λ' (or 'rps · token profile · arrival rate λ'), so the box agrees with §6.1.1 and with the caption; then delete the caption's 'Label caveat' paragraph, since the caveat exists only to explain the mismatch. If the box must keep 'concurrency', move it out of the Workload box and draw it on the serving/scheduler side as a derived quantity (in-flight = λ × W).

findings.evidence: PDF p.153 (book p.129): "We see: p95 TTFT climbing (serving), KV cache hit ratio low (resource: FLOP/reuse — prefill recomputation), and prefill queue depth growing" — but the same chapter's mini-case (PDF p.157) reads "low prefix-hit ratio", §6.6 (PDF p.156) reads "Prefix-cache hit rates", and Ch. 2's vocabulary table (PDF p.44) explicitly separates "KV cache" ("not an optimization over a shared prefix") from "prefix caching / KV reuse" ("reusing already-computed K/V for a shared prefix, to skip re-prefilling it").
findings.issue: Terminology drift on a repeated diagnostic metric: 'KV cache hit ratio' names the stored-state object, but the quantity meant (and glossed inline as 'FLOP/reuse — prefill recomputation') is the prefix-cache hit ratio. The book's own Ch. 2 vocabulary table and Preface ('load-bearing contrasts are never relaxed') require the two terms to stay distinct, yet Ch. 6 uses both names for the same counter within four pages.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace 'KV cache hit ratio' in §6.3.4 with 'prefix-cache hit ratio' (the normative term per Ch. 2's vocabulary table, §6.6 and the §6.8 mini-case), then sweep Chapter 6 for any further instances of the 'KV cache hit' phrasing.
